questions.title: What constitutes ‘pending’ or ‘reasonably anticipated’ enforcement proceedings under § 552(b)(7)(A)?
questions.question_body:
In *Foad Farahi v. FBI*, the court found FBI’s investigation was still ’ongoing’ more than three years after the initial request—even though there was no formal indictment against Mr. Farahi yet.

I’m unclear how courts determine whether an investigation satisfies ‘pending’ or ‘reasonably anticipated’. Do you need an indictment, trial docket, or conviction?

* How do appellate courts apply *CREW* 746 F. 3d 1082’s “ongoing criminal investigations count as ’proceedings’ ” standard?

* Does an immigration removal proceeding qualify as a forceful “enforcement proceeding”?

* What are the evidentiary requirements—based on affidavits, internal memos—or civil judgments required to establish pendency when only an affidavit supports it?

* Why did Judge Katsas rely primarily on changes in FBI’s operatives’ statements (Bender’s confirmation March 2023) rather than direct evidence contrary to earlier determinations?

questions.title: "Deferential scrutiny" applies specifically in Exempt‑(OIC—But also should policy updates continue after denials?
questions.question_body:
"Because the FBI specializes… official endorsement… entitled fair measure of deference"—the Court emphasizes it at several points including *Campbell v. DOJ*.

I understand general administrative‑law deference rules (e.g., Chevron), but why does § 552(b)(7)(A) demand higher deference?

* Which judicial standard governs agency determinations on Ex‑(OIC)—Rational Basis versus Strict Scrutiny—and why?

* How does national‑security context shift liability sidelining First Amendment concerns like freedom of expression?

* How has precedent evolved—from *Mead Data central*, *Juarez*, and *CNSS*—to support stronger agency credibility for counterterrorism investigations?

questions.title: "Segregation” Requirement Under § 552(a)(8)(A)(ii)– Is Whole Record Withholding Mandatory?
questions.question_body:
*Farahi* emphasized only limited bits might be releasable—mostly random words interspersed through CDs.

I’d like clarification:

* What makes segregability reasonable versus unreasonable per *Mead*, *Juarez*, *Perioperative Services*, especially when documents are physical CDs rather than typed pages?

* When would “inextricably intertwined” extend beyond obvious redacting boundaries—e.g., if exempt portions inform context for non‑exempt statements?

* Are there procedural steps agencies must take before positive conclusions—e.g., naming threatened parties—or can they rely solely on an affidavit plus internal memo?

questions.title: "Category” Identification Under § 552(b)– Why Must Agencies Use Specific Distinct Categories?
questions.question_body:
*Farahi* raised that excluded categories appeared overbroad because he never saw particular definitions.

I noted *CREW*, *Gallant*, and *Khine v. DHS*’s utility lists stating categories must enable courts identify applicable exemptions.

My confusions:

* What minimum level of detail distinguishes one category from another?

* If every page has both exempt information (evidence) and potential public interest facts, can any single category suffice? Or must agencies split these individually before affording partial release?

* How does failure to meet categorize expectations affect withdrawal credibility?

questions.title: "Ex Parte" Declarations—When Are They Acceptable?
questions.question_body:
*Farahi* protested reliance upon sealed Hardy/Bender affidavits.

Is it legitimate for plaintiffs to challenge Secretary‐issued sealed submissions once a motion was approved without prejudice?

In particular:

* Under what circumstances does a summarizable request mandate presentation only in secret because disclosure jeopardizes interests listed in Section12(c),(k)?

* Does denying appellants any chance substitutes escalatory demands such as judicial notice limits—per *Perioperative Services*, "the problem is inherent" comment—or is there alternative means for verifying facts before adjudication?
